source.version: Target journal paper: abstract only (Crossref, DOI 10.1177/26339137241305117; bibliographic metadata and abstract read 2026-10-09). No full text of the target paper was obtained. The complete local markdown and relevant PDF pages, including Appendix A, were also read at C:/Dropbox/Research/ai-lab/literature/creativity/Heyman et al (2024) - Supermind Ideator.md and the corresponding .pdf path. Despite their filename and retrieval association, these files contain arXiv:2311.01937v1, dated 3 November 2023 on PDF p. 1, titled Supermind Ideator: Exploring generative AI to support creative problem-solving, with Steven R. Rick and Gianni Giacomelli as the first authors. This is an earlier system description, not the target experimental paper. Its 40-person formative usability study (PDF p. 5, section 5) is not used as the target experiment's sample. SAGE journal and erratum access and the ACM conference PDF returned HTTP 403; the MIT repository conference PDF required human verification (HTTP 405). The later experiment and the erratum could not be checked in full text. The study below is coded solely from the target journal abstract.
source.title_on_document: Supermind Ideator: How scaffolding Human-AI collaboration can increase creativity

paper_design_summary: The target journal abstract describes an experiment comparing people using Supermind Ideator, people using ChatGPT, and people working alone on creative problem-solving. It reports greater innovativeness of ideas generated by Supermind Ideator users, but gives no assignment mechanism, participant counts, scoring method, or numerical results. The retrieved local full text is a differently titled earlier system description and cannot establish these details for the target experiment.

eligibility.reason: Core eligibility is unclear: the target Crossref abstract reports an experiment and an innovativeness result on ideas generated by people using Supermind Ideator, ChatGPT, or working alone, supporting the output-outcome criterion, but it states neither random allocation nor the number of people analyzed. The random-assignment criterion and the threshold of at least 50 analyzed people therefore remain unresolved (Crossref abstract, DOI 10.1177/26339137241305117, results sentence; https://api.crossref.org/works/10.1177/26339137241305117; read 2026-10-09). The local PDF is the differently titled earlier arXiv:2311.01937v1 system description (PDF p. 1, title and version). Its formative study with 40 professionals and qualitative usability/applicability feedback (PDF p. 5, section 5, Evaluation) cannot establish the target experiment's assignment or sample size. The target full text and erratum remain unverified. The accessible evidence does not establish nonrandom allocation or any of the context classes; context_class remains none.

one_line_finding: The target journal abstract reports significantly more innovative ideas with Supermind Ideator than with ChatGPT or working alone, but supplies no numerical result, participant count, or assignment mechanism (Crossref abstract, DOI 10.1177/26339137241305117).
